plans.title: Halo Laser 7-Day Recovery Plan
plans.disclaimer: This is general wellness information and is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Follow your licensed provider's instructions and contact them with clinical questions or concerns.

days.whats_common: Many patients notice warmth, redness, tightness, and a sunburn-like feeling during the first day after a Halo laser treatment.
days.watch_for: If you notice rapidly worsening pain, spreading swelling, fever, pus-like drainage, or symptoms that feel concerning, it's worth reaching out to your provider.
days.suggested_action: Consider saving a Day 1 baseline recovery note or photo in Track Procedure if your provider has said photo tracking is appropriate.

reminder.title: Halo Day 1 recovery check-in
reminder.body: Consider adding a gentle recovery note or baseline photo if photo tracking is appropriate for you.

days.whats_common: It's common around this time for redness, swelling, tightness, and sensitivity to remain visible while the skin barrier is still settling.
days.watch_for: If swelling becomes asymmetric, vision feels affected, discomfort escalates sharply, or the treated area looks infected, it's worth reaching out to your provider.
days.suggested_action: Consider logging how your skin feels today so future progress comparisons have more context.

reminder.title: Halo Day 2 recovery note
reminder.body: Consider logging today's recovery context, such as comfort, redness, and swelling.

days.whats_common: Many patients start noticing a dry, rough, sandpapery texture as surface renewal becomes more obvious.
days.watch_for: If cracking, bleeding, severe itching, unusual drainage, or intense tenderness appears, it's worth reaching out to your provider.
days.suggested_action: Consider taking your next Track Procedure scan today if lighting and framing can match your baseline.

reminder.title: Halo Day 3 tracking scan
reminder.body: Consider taking a matched-lighting progress scan for your Halo recovery record.

days.whats_common: It's common around now for dryness and visible texture to peak for some patients, while redness may gradually begin to soften.
days.watch_for: If the recovery pattern suddenly worsens after improving, or if new severe pain, swelling, or heat develops, it's worth reaching out to your provider.
days.suggested_action: Consider reviewing your recovery trend notes rather than relying on a single day's appearance.

reminder.title: Halo Day 4 recovery context
reminder.body: Consider adding a short note about texture, redness, and comfort today.

days.whats_common: Many patients notice flaking or a bronzed, rough surface appearance during this part of recovery.
days.watch_for: If the skin appears increasingly raw, has open areas, or shows signs that feel outside your provider's expected course, it's worth reaching out to your provider.
days.suggested_action: Consider adding a progress note or photo only if it can be captured gently and consistently.

reminder.title: Halo Day 5 recovery note
reminder.body: Consider recording today's texture and comfort level in your procedure timeline.

days.whats_common: It's common for visible roughness to continue improving gradually, though redness or sensitivity may still be present.
days.watch_for: If irritation is escalating, sensitivity feels severe, or recovery seems to move backward instead of gradually settling, it's worth reaching out to your provider.
days.suggested_action: Consider checking whether your recent notes and photos show a steady overall direction rather than judging a single snapshot.

reminder.title: Halo Day 6 recovery check-in
reminder.body: Consider checking your recent notes and photos for overall recovery direction.

days.whats_common: Many patients are past the most intense early texture phase by the end of the first week, while color and sensitivity can continue to normalize over time.
days.watch_for: If redness, swelling, drainage, pain, or sensitivity feels concerning or outside your provider's expected timeline, it's worth reaching out to your provider.
days.suggested_action: Consider taking a Day 7 Track Procedure scan to document the first-week recovery point if conditions can match your earlier scan.

reminder.title: Halo Day 7 tracking scan
reminder.body: Consider taking a matched-lighting Day 7 scan for your Halo recovery record.
